title: A Generalisation Signal Need Not Be a Model-Selection Signal
abstract: arXiv:2609.39099v1 Announce Type: cross  Abstract: Model selection in computational biology often relies on validation data drawn from the training regime, even when deployment lies outside it. When validation no longer preserves which model is best, a natural alternative is to rank candidates using properties of the trained network itself. We test this idea using a novel, forward-only proxy motivated by the norm of the Hessian, alongside common Hessian measures, across molecular property, protein fitness, and drug-response tasks. Contrary to our hypothesis, geometry does not become more useful as validation Spearman correlation deteriorates: augmenting validation helps some shifts but significantly harms others. More surprisingly, the proxy still correlates with generalisation gap on most tasks even when Hessian trace and top-eigenvalue relationships are weak or reversed, yet this signal does not reliably identify the deployment-best model. translated_title: 泛化信号未必是模型选择信号
translated_abstract: 计算生物学中的模型选择通常依赖于从训练环境中抽取的验证数据，即使部署环境超出了该范围。当验证数据不再能保留哪个模型最优的信息时，一个自然的替代方法是利用训练好的网络本身的属性来对候选模型进行排序。我们使用一种受Hessian范数启发的新型仅前向传播代理指标，结合常见的Hessian度量指标，在分子性质、蛋白质适应度和药物反应任务上测试了这一想法。与我们的假设相反，随着验证Spearman相关性的恶化，几何指标并没有变得更有用：增强验证对某些分布偏移有帮助，但对另一些则有显著损害。更令人惊讶的是，即使在Hessian迹和顶部特征值关系较弱或发生反转的情况下，该代理指标在大多数任务上仍与泛化差距相关，然而这一信号并不能可靠地识别出部署环境下最优的模型。曲率界不必保留跨分布的模型排序信息。
tldr: 该研究发现，尽管受Hessian启发的新型仅前向传播代理指标在大多数任务上与泛化差距相关，但这种泛化信号并不能可靠地识别出部署环境下最优的模型，表明泛化信号未必能作为模型选择的信号。
en_tdlr: This study finds that although a novel Hessian-inspired forward-only proxy still correlates with generalisation gap on most tasks, this signal does not reliably identify the deployment-best model, demonstrating that a generalisation signal need not serve as a model-selection signal.
